analysis:
The PR adds `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` (repeatable) for putting sandbox VM images and jobs on external APFS drives. It touches docs, the changelog, Swift sources (SandboxInstaller, SandboxSetupCommand, SandboxWorkDisk, SandboxEligibility, SandboxAddon, SandboxSetupProgress) and tests. Relevant boundary: TB-013/T-061 (CLI downloads and runs install.sh and the add-on as the Mac owner, A-019). T-041 covers external cache volumes separately, and the sandbox work disks are a different data path.

Reviewed from the supplied units:
- Installer arguments are built as an argv array (`sizingArguments` appends `--disk` and the path) and run via /bin/sh with the script path. No shell-string interpolation is visible, so there is no injection path. The download validation is unchanged: HTTPS only, HTTPS-only redirects, 1 MiB cap, shebang check.
- `supportsDisks` is a substring capability probe on the downloaded script, the same trust model as `supportsPlan`. It adds no trust and no control. Setup refuses `--disk` with a script that does not name it, before any change.
- The privileged step, `sudo diskutil enableOwnership <mount>`, runs only at an interactive prompt, never with `--yes`, and only after an explicit default-no confirmation. SandboxWorkDisk.enableOwnership spawns /usr/bin/sudo by absolute path with `--`. The mount point comes from statfs. The CLI never reads the password. A /Volumes/<name> symlink to another volume is rejected by the mount-point match, and the installer rechecks each disk.
- Add-on status and plan JSON `disks` parsing is typed and tolerant; malformed entries are dropped. The values are only displayed, and add-on and installer output was already trusted terminal text under T-061.
- Tests and fakes are not shipped.

Residual gaps, not findings:
- SandboxWorkDisk.absolutePath and the installer argument ordering were not fully visible, so option injection through a path beginning with `-` is unverified. Passing the path as a separate argv element makes it a low risk.
- Control characters in hostile volume labels printed to the terminal are unverified.
- The threat model (TB-013/A-019) should note that VM images and jobs may live on external drives outside the attested boundary, with the same peripheral caveats as T-041.

No concrete regression was established. The 59 omitted integration source units mean the replay was incomplete.
